record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: For Wigner ensembles whose equilibrium measure changes topology as parameters vary, can one analyze and control the critical regimes where intervals in the support of the equilibrium measure open, close, or merge, including the associated local universality classes?

evidence.quote: Furthermore, one would like to analyze and control situations where parameters in the underlying matrix distributions vary, and intervals in the support of the equilibrium distribution for the ensemble open and close.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider unitary-invariant (or more generally Wigner-type) random matrix ensembles on the space of N×N Hermitian matrices with joint eigenvalue density proportional to
  ∏_{i<j} (x_i - x_j)^2  exp(-N ∑_i V(x_i; t)),
where V(·; t) is a real-analytic external potential depending on a parameter (or parameters) t. As N → ∞, the empirical spectral distribution converges weakly to an equilibrium measure μ_t which minimizes the logarithmic energy functional
  E[μ] = ∫∫ log(1/|x-y|) dμ(x) dμ(y) + ∫ V(x; t) dμ(x).
Generically the support supp(μ_t) consists of finitely many disjoint intervals, but as t varies critical parameter values t* may occur at which:
 (a) a new interval opens (birth of a band),
 (b) an interval closes (a band shrinks to a point), or
 (c) two adjacent intervals merge at an interior endpoint.

Problem: Develop a rigorous asymptotic analysis, uniform in a neighbourhood of every such critical parameter t*, of the local eigenvalue statistics for these ensembles. Specifically, identify and prove the local universality classes (and the corresponding limiting correlation kernels) that arise in each of the three critical scenarios (band opening, band closing, band merging), determine the appropriate double-scaling regimes in (N, t-t*), and establish that the limiting kernels (such as those built from Painlevé II / Hastings–McLeod, Pearcey, or related integrable kernels) are universal across the class of admissible potentials V(·; t) producing the same type of critical transition. The analysis should also control the transition between the critical kernel and the generic bulk/edge (sine/Airy) kernels away from the critical point.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress exists for the unitary-invariant case: double-scaling limits at band-closing critical points yield the Hastings–McLeod (Painlevé II) kernel (Bleher–Its, Claeys–Kuijlaars), band-merging gives the Pearcey kernel (Brézin–Hikami, Bertola–Cafasso), and openness of regular regimes has been established (Bertola, 2022). Phase transitions and equilibrium measures have been classified for polynomial potentials (Martínez-Finkelshtein–Silva, 2014). However, a complete uniform analysis and universality across all Wigner-type (not just invariant) ensembles in all three transition scenarios remains incomplete, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Openness of Regular Regimes of Complex Random Matrix Models
status_evidence.snippet: Openness of regular regimes of complex random matrix models, addressing parameter variation in equilibrium measures.
status_evidence.claim: Regular regimes are open under parameter variation, supporting partial progress on critical transitions.

status_evidence.title: Phase transitions and equilibrium measures in random matrix models
status_evidence.snippet: Studies families of equilibrium measures in a polynomial external field, classifying phase transitions.
status_evidence.claim: Critical regimes for opening/closing/merging of bands have been analyzed in the polynomial-potential invariant case.

status_evidence.title: Universality of the double scaling limit in random matrix models
status_evidence.snippet: Universality of the eigenvalue correlation kernel at critical points constructed from Painlevé II functions.
status_evidence.claim: Double-scaling universality at band-closing critical points is known (Painlevé II / Hastings–McLeod kernel).
